title: Ship Fast, Ship Safe — Positioning Brief
content:
Purpose

Quick internal brief to surface a concise, execution-friendly narrative that answers: why should engineers and platform teams pick Redwood for shipping LLM features under production constraints? This is a working one-pager for sales enablement, docs heads, and product marketers to iterate on.

Core mission statement (single line)

Make running inference predictable and low-risk for engineering teams that need to ship quickly without second-guessing reliability or unit economics.

Thesis (2–3 sentences)

As models proliferate, control and differentiation shift from model selection to how reliably and economically those models run in production. Teams that can ship features quickly while meeting latency, cost, and compliance targets capture product-led adoption. Redwood is the runtime and ops layer that lets engineering orgs move from experimentation to consistent production deliverables.

Why Redwood (elevator answer)

Redwood unblocks teams that want to deliver LLM functionality without building or babysitting inference infra: predictable latency and cost controls, built-in fallbacks for graceful degradation, and developer ergonomics that match modern engineering workflows (APIs, SDKs, rollouts).

Positioning pillars (short, actionable)

1) Predictable economics at scale — unit-cost controls, intelligent batching and cache suggestions, transparent token-level billing so product managers and finance can forecast spend.
2) Performance that degrades gracefully — automated fallback model routing, regional failover, and configurable SLO-driven policies that prevent user-visible outages.
3) Developer-first control plane — same API and tooling across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments so teams can iterate locally and scale without replatforming.

Key differentiators to call out in GTM materials

- Runtime-first: not just managed endpoints, but an inference engine that optimizes kernels, KV cache, and batching for real traffic patterns.
- Cross-environment parity: policies, rollouts, and observability work identically in hosted or private deployments.
- Cost engineering as a feature: tooling that surfaces batching/caching/quantization tradeoffs and the expected unit-economics impact.
- Safety net ops: automatic fallbacks and per-route latency guards that keep products responsive under load or degraded model capacity.

Competitive notes (short analysis)

- Major cloud AI providers: strong on model catalog and integration with cloud stack; weaker on predictable unit economics and on-prem parity. Position: Redwood is the choice when predictable cost and multi-environment parity matter.
- API-first LLM vendors: simpler API but limited controls for latency SLOs and rollout policies at scale. Position: Redwood keeps the easy API while exposing ops levers for production.
- Self-hosted inference stacks / OSS runtimes: high control but heavy ops burden. Position: Redwood offloads the undifferentiated ops while keeping advanced runtime knobs and private deployment options.

Target personas & headline hooks

- ML Engineer / Model Ops: "Ship model-backed features with reproducible latency and predictable cost — keep your experiments and production behavior aligned."
- Platform / Infra Lead: "Standardize inference across teams with a single control plane for rollouts, tracing, and SLOs — avoid 50 different endpoint patterns."
- Product Engineer / PM: "Deliver product features on schedule with confidence: latency and spend won’t surprise your go-to-market plan."

Sample short pitches (for docs, sales one-liners)

- "From prototype to production: consistent latency, predictable spend, and the same API whether you run in our cloud or your VPC."
- "We tune serving, not just models — batching, caching, and fallbacks reduce cost and keep experiences snappy."

Objections and rebuttals (quick)

- "We can just self-host to save costs." — Self-hosting hides ops complexity; Redwood reduces both capex and ongoing engineering cycles with off-the-shelf runtime optimizations and rollout safety nets while offering private deployments when needed.
- "Cloud provider managed endpoints are fine for us." — Managed endpoints are convenient but often opaque on unit economics and inconsistent across regions and private setups; Redwood provides transparent token-level costing and deployment parity.
- "We don't want vendor lock-in." — Redwood exposes the same API and model variants you can run in dedicated or private modes; we emphasize portability and clear escape hatches in contracts and tooling.

Proof points & suggested metrics to publish

- 30–60% reduction in tokens/second cost on typical customer prompts when enabling caching + batching recommendations (anonymized case study).
-99.9% availability for dedicated customers with canary rollouts and automated fallback policies.
- Median p95 latency targets by model family and region (transparent benchmark table to include in technical appendix).

Go-to-market uses for this asset

- Sales one-pager for engineering buyers and platform leads.
- Core homepage copy and hero experiment (A/B test variant).
- Internal pitch deck slide and SDR excerpt.

Next steps & asks

- Ask: PMs and product marketing to produce a trimmed 2-line hero and a 60-word subhead for web.
- Ask: Solutions eng to share two anonymized customer case metrics we can publish on cost and availability by Feb 12.
- Ask: Research to provide a short p95 latency benchmark for three representative open models by Feb 5.

Open questions / tradeoffs

- How aggressively do we commit to specific % cost savings in public collateral? Risk vs. credibility — prefer conservative, verifiable numbers.
- Messaging tone: engineering-technical (deep runtime proofs) vs. product/business (cost/time-to-market). Recommend two variants for testing: technical for platform pages, business for homepage and SDRs.

Author notes

This is intentionally compact and tactical. It should be used as the single-source draft for creating a one-page web hero, a technical appendix for sales, and a short internal FAQ. Iterations welcome — comment inline on Confluence margin or drop edits to JIRA-RT-4123.
